To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

known allergen structures can be used to accurately predict IgE responses to parasite allergen-like (parallergen) proteins and that serological processes typically seen with allergens also occur with parallergens.

known allergen structures were used to predict IgG and IgE binding antigens in Schistosomiasis and that IgG4 and down-regulation of the IgE response were observed in response to increased Schistosomia mansoni egg antigen exposure, mirroring responses to allergens.
the IgE response to S. mansoni is directed to a limited number of protein families, and that the structures of known allergen proteins can be used to identify these families.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
allergen-like proteins (parallergen) can be predicted in metazoan infections and that they are recognized by IgE in infected individuals.

the IgE response to S. mansoni infection is not only directed against a small number of allergen-like proteins but also that the serological response is dominated by IgE/IgE/IgG1/IgG4 responses against these proteins.
the allergenicity of a protein depends on the protein family to which it belongs, and not on the species of the host or the protein itself.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified 12 parallergens (10 allergen-like proteins, 2 novel Pfam domain families) in S. mansonisome of which are likely to be important in the IgE responses of infected individuals.

we have shown that the structures of known allergen families can be used to identify allergen-like proteins (parallergen) in S. mansonis and that the IgE/Ig4 responses against parallergens are regulated in a manner similar to allergens.

the IgE response to S. mansoni is directed against a small number of protein domain families that are highly conserved across metazoans and that are also found in the major environmental allergen protein families.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IgE binding in helminth infections is not random, as has been assumed in the past.

allergenicity can be defined as the presence of certain protein domain structures in metazoan proteins and that this definition is applicable to both allergens and their homologues in metazoan parasite proteins (parallergenic proteins).
the structures of known allergen domains (Pfam) can be used to find IgE responses to homologous proteins in metazoans, including parasites.
